Subject: Performance SLO & Autoscaling follow-up (FinLytics)

Hi Alex / Samir,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on performance/SLO requirements and how Redwood would handle autoscaling/burst capacity for your inference workloads.

Call highlights (high level):
- Target p95 latency: 150ms for single-turn text-generation requests (80-120 tokens typical).
- Throughput target: sustained 200 req/s during business hours, with bursts up to 1,200 req/s for 30-60s during market events.
- Concurrency: expected ~50 concurrent sessions; streaming enabled for 35% of requests.
- SLO: 99.9% availability and 95% of requests under the p95 latency target during sustained traffic; during burst windows allow degraded budget but must not exceed 2s for streamed responses.

Autoscaling/behavior items we discussed:
- Warm pool: maintain a warm pool equivalent to ~250 req/s capacity to cover steady growth and reduce cold-starts.
- Scale-up times: typical scale-up to full reserved nodes within 60-90s; fast-burst buffer (warm pool + request queuing) to absorb short spikes under 30s.
- Queueing policy: short TTL queue with priority for interactive sessions; token-rate shaping for long generation jobs.

Next steps:
1) I attached a draft SLO matrix (20261120-slo-matrix.xlsx) that maps your targets to Redwood config recommendations, please review and flag anything missing.
2) Rishi will follow up with a short config sketch for warm-pool sizing and estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted cost for the profile above.
3) We'll run a short load validation (30m) on a representative workload before procurement to validate scale-up times and tail latency.

Action items:
- Alex: confirm the p95 latency target and expected token-length distribution (short/medium/long).
- Samir: confirm which routes require streaming vs non-streaming.
- Rishi: provide warm pool sizing and cost delta by Mon (23 Nov).

Attachments: 20261120-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO matrix, recommended configs)

Thanks, looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Autoscaling follow-up (FinLytics)

Alex,

Great questions. Quick answers inline then some detail below.

1) Streaming per-token latency: Redwood provides token-level metrics for streaming sessions (avg, p50/p95/p99 per token) and an end-to-end stream latency metric. We can include a sampling dashboard for your routes during the validation run.

2) Burst routing / failover: by default our smart routing will try the primary region; on saturation it can fail over to a configured secondary region (EU/NA split) with route-level policy. Fallbacks will respect your data residency settings; we can engineer an approver flow if EU-only data is required.

More detail on autoscale behavior:
- Warm pools: we recommend an initial warm pool sized to ~30-40% of your peak burst capacity (so for 1,200 req/s peak, a ~360-480 req/s warm pool). That reduces the amount of rapid node spin-up required and keeps per-token tail latency low.
- Scale-up timeline: for the model variants we discussed, a full node spin-up (cold) is ~120-180s; however with a warm pool + pre-warmed kernels we typically observe effective capacity creation in ~45-75s for the remaining delta.
- Short bursts <30s: absorbed by warm pool + short request queue (TTL 10-20s). For longer sustained bursts we scale nodes and can shift lower-priority batch jobs off the cluster.
- Queue policy: interactive sessions get higher priority and shorter TTL; heavy batch or low-priority jobs are deprioritized automatically.

I've uploaded a short design doc (redwood-autoscale-design.pdf) and updated the SLO matrix with recommended warm pool numbers and expected latency bands. Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/FinLytics/SLO-matrix

Rishi / Monica, can you confirm the warm pool sizing math matches our Dedicated sizing calc and whether we should propose a two-zone warm pool (split across AZs) for lower RTO? Also can you add an estimate for the validation run (approx vCPU/GPU hours)?

Alex / Samir, please let us know if the warm-pool percentage above sounds acceptable or if you prefer we propose both a Hosted and Dedicated cost comparison.

Best,
Marissa

- Warm-pool sizing: recommend we propose both 360 req/s (30% of 1,200) and 480 req/s (40%) scenarios. Include two-zone split (50/50) to reduce AZ-risk.
- Cost delta: preliminary estimate suggests Dedicated reserved nodes (monthly commit) will be ~18-25% cheaper for your sustained 200 req/s baseline, but Hosted remains >30% cheaper for low-commit scenarios with heavy bursting due to our burst buffer features. Need to run precise calc against the SLO matrix tokens.
- Validation run: 30m load test approximates to 1.2 GPU-hours (peak) plus 4 CPU-hours for traffic shaping / collectors; we'll include standard monitoring hooks and token-trace sampling.
